audit.whatIsWrong: The tldr and report[0].t both asserted in capitals that 'Wind Wall does NOT block soldier autos'. That is the single most important interaction in the matchup and it is stated backwards.
audit.why: Wind Wall 'blocks all enemy projectiles for 4 seconds' and carries blocksProjectiles ('deletes enemy projectile damage entirely'). Azir's Sand Soldier attacks are line projectiles — 'Their attacks deal magic damage to enemies in a line'. Wind Wall eats them. The run brief lists this exact gap in its calibration examples: Azir vs Yasuo never mentioned Wind Wall blocking Azir's soldier attacks.
audit.corrected: tldr and report[0].t rewritten to say Wind Wall DOES block soldier attacks, with the 4-second duration and the 25s rank-1 cooldown. Reinforced in breakdown.early, breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t, loading, whys[2] and content mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer gave Yasuo all seven rows while the content layer and the packet chart both gave Azir the last three. Three rows rendered two different answers.
audit.why: Win rate is 52.55% over 1488 games — Azir is the favoured side overall, and both the packet chart and the content layer place the flip at level 6. Emperor's Divide is the mechanism: Sweeping Blade needs a path and Last Breath needs an Airborne target, and 120s of terrain across the approach denies the first and therefore the second.
audit.corrected: full phases[4..6].side moved Yasuo->Azir with each why rewritten in the same proposal. content win[] already matched the packet and was left alone.

audit.whatIsWrong: Not one spike or phase carried a cooldown, and spikes[2] was pure template.
audit.why: The numbers that matter are all in the kits: Wind Wall 25/23/21/19/17s for 4 seconds, Last Breath 70/50/30s, Sweeping Blade 0.5s down to 0.1s, Emperor's Divide 120/105/90s. Steel Tempest is 'treated as a basic attack and scales with all the same things', so his crit items scale the poke as well as the all-in.
audit.corrected: Cooldowns written into spikes[1], phases[4..6].why, breakdown.cooldowns, breakdown.mid, breakdown.feeding, report[9].t and loading. spikes[2] regrounded on Steel Tempest scaling as a basic attack.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit — defect catalogue item 3. dontsFull[1].d also cited a nineteen-second Shifting Sands.
audit.why: Wind Wall's 25s rank-1 cooldown against a 4-second duration is the whole sequencing rule of this lane and it was written as 'hold your poke until it is spent'. Shifting Sands is 22s at rank 1; 19s is rank 3.
audit.corrected: Rewrote with Wind Wall 25/23/21/19/17s and its 21 seconds of rank-1 downtime, Last Breath 70s falling to 30s, and Shifting Sands 22s. dontsFull[1].d corrected to 22s.

audit.whatIsWrong: tradeBad claimed 'the engage window every Yasuo player is waiting for' and never mentioned the shield that eats chip poke.
audit.why: Way of the Wanderer 'builds toward a shield whenever he is moving. The shield triggers when he takes damage from a champion or monster' — chip poke into a walking Yasuo is absorbed. Trades have to be committed, not dribbled out.
audit.corrected: tradeBad, breakdown.trading and report[3].t rewritten around the Flow shield; tradeGood rewritten around trading only in the Wind Wall downtime.

audit.whatIsWrong: Copy-paste bleed: dosFull[1].d was the tradeGood string verbatim under the title 'Wall his EQ-knockup engage with R', and dontsFull[2].d was the tradeBad string verbatim under 'Waste the wall on a half-committed engage'. dosFull[0].d and dosFull[2].d also explained something other than their titles. wants.you[1] said he dashes in 'with Steel Tempest' — the dash is Sweeping Blade; Riot's Q text is 'Thrusts forward'.
audit.why: Defect catalogue item 2, plus an ability mix-up between Q and E.
audit.corrected: All five bodies rewritten against their own titles; wants.you[1] corrected to Sweeping Blade.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.wave recommended a controlled slow push, which is the worst wave state against a champion whose mobility runs on having units to dash through.
audit.why: Sweeping Blade 'dashes through target enemy' and 'cannot be re-cast on the same enemy for a few seconds' — a big wave between you is a corridor of fresh dash targets and free Steel Tempest stacks. A thin wave takes that away.
audit.corrected: Rewritten around fast crashes and crashing on the Wind Wall cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: enemyWin, ahead, breakdown.early, breakdown.mid, breakdown.carry, breakdown.feeding and breakdown.late were name-swap templates.
audit.why: Template sweep — each would read identically against any other mid laner with the name changed.
audit.corrected: Each regrounded on the two things that are specific to Yasuo: Wind Wall deleting soldier attacks, and Last Breath requiring an Airborne target that only the two-stack Steel Tempest provides.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page states in five places that Yasuo can Sweeping Blade through Azir's Sand Soldiers. I could not verify from the kit whether Sand Soldiers are valid dash targets for an enemy.
audit.why: Riot's E text says only 'Dashes through target enemy'. Whether Azir's Sand Soldiers count as targetable enemy units is exactly the kind of thing the kit file leaves empty, and empty means unknown, not no.
audit.corrected: No edit made. spikes[0].text, content early, content late, wants.you[0] and wants.foe[0] left exactly as they are. Where I needed to write about the same idea I phrased it as denying him a path rather than denying him a soldier — see spikes[1], spikes[3] and dosFull[1].d.

notes: The headline fix: tldr and report[0].t asserted in capitals that Wind Wall does NOT block soldier autos. It does — Riot's W text is 'blocks all enemy projectiles for 4 seconds', the kit flag reads 'deletes enemy projectile damage entirely', and Azir's soldier attacks 'deal magic damage to enemies in a line'. This is also listed in the run brief's own calibration examples. Both fields now say so with the 25s rank-1 cooldown and the 21 seconds of downtime it leaves. Chart: full phases[4..6].side moved Yasuo->Azir with whys, matching the packet and content layers. Ratings left untouched — polarity ambiguous, see questionsForUser. packet.suspectNames flagged "Sweeping Blade's" in spikes[1] as a probable wrong name: false positive, the kit confirms E is Sweeping Blade. Two derived-flag misfires I did not build on: Yasuo's Wind Wall carries a 'terrain: blocks paths and dashes' flag, but Riot's text says only that it blocks projectiles, so I wrote nothing about it stopping your Shifting Sands; and Steel Tempest carries a 'dash' flag while Riot's text says 'Thrusts forward', so I corrected wants.you[1] to name Sweeping Blade as the dash instead. Left deliberately untouched: five fields state that Yasuo can Sweeping Blade through Azir's Sand Soldiers (spikes[0].text, content early, content late, wants.you[0], wants.foe[0]). Riot's E text says only 'Dashes through target enemy' and the kit does not say whether Sand Soldiers are valid enemy targets — see unverified.
